newsitem.title: USA: Florida cogeneration plants file for bankruptcy.
newsitem.headline: Florida cogeneration plants file for bankruptcy.

text.p: Three partnerships, owners of what they call the world's largest biomass cogeneration plants, said Wednesday they have filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection.

The partnerships owned by Pacific Gas & Electric Co and Bechtel said the filing was necessary because Florida Power & Light Co had notified them it would unilaterally terminate the litigation standstill agreement in place since early February.
This agreement was reached after the FPL Group Inc unit filed suit January 8 to avoid its obligations under power purchase contracts it signed in 1991, the partnerships said.
The standstill agreement put the utility's suit on hold while it attempted to negotiate a settlement with the owners of the cogeneration plants, a Florida Power spokeswoman said.
The 70 megawatt plant in Okeelanta and a 55 megawatt plant in Oceola -- communities in western Palm Beach County, Fla. -- are owned equally by U.S. Generating and Flo-Sun Inc.
U.S. Generating is jointly owned by units of Bechtel and PG&E Corp, the holding company formed earlier this year by Pacific Gas.
Flo-Sun owns sugar plants that use steam produced by the cogeneration plants.
The sugar plants produce the bagasse -- what is left of the sugar cane after the sugar is removed -- that is used along with wood waste to fuel the plants.
The plants delivered electricity to FPL during 1996 and have been operating in accordance with their respective power sales contracts, the partnerships said.

In a statement explaining the filing, they said "We consider FPL's suit to be without merit," and pointed out FPL's power purchase contracts were not mandated. Instead, they are "standard-offer" power sales contracts presented to FPL in response to its requests for power in the early 1990s.

A spokesman for the partnerships said the plants offered FPL the lowest cost power avialable at the time the contracts were signed but declined to say what the utility is paying for power generated by the plants.

He said the Okeelanta plant is owned by Okeelanta Power LP and the Osceola plant is owned by Gator Generating Co LP. A third partnership filing for bankruptcy protection, Osceola Power LP, was involved in building the Osceola plant.
The three partnerships, in turn, are owned by U.S. Generating and Flo-Sun.
The partnerships said their bankruptcy petition was filed Wednesday morning in the West Palm Beach Division of the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of Florida.
They said more than $350 million was invested in project development, environmental permitting, financing and plant construction, based on FPL's contractual commitments.

This was financed, in part, through Palm Beach County's issuance by of its Solid Waste Industrial Development Revenue Bonds (Okeelanta Power Limited Partnership Project) Series 1993A, originally issued in an aggregate principal amount of $160 million, and its Solid Waste Industrial Development Revenue Bonds (Osceola Power Limited Partnership Project), which were issued in two series -- the Exempt Facility Series 1994A, issued in an aggregate principal amount of $120.5 million and the Taxable Series 1994B, issued in an aggregate principal amount of $8 million.
